title: California Youth Substance Use: Vaping & Marijuana

sources.title: SAMHSA – National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH)
California Department of Public Health, SAPB

facts.title: Nicotine Vaping Among California Teens
facts.description: Approximately 14.5% of California high school students reported current e-cigarette use
facts.trend: Declining from 2019 peak of 27% (CHKS data shows 56% reduction since 2019)

facts.title: Marijuana Use Among CA Teens
facts.description: 11.2% of California adolescents reported using marijuana in the past 30 days

facts.title: Marijuana Vaping Prevalence
facts.description: 7.3% of California high school students reported vaping marijuana (THC products)

facts.title: Youth Who Start Vaping Nicotine Before Age 18
facts.description: 8 in 10 adults who currently vape nicotine started before age 18, establishing early addiction patterns
facts.trend: Highlights critical intervention window during middle & high school years

facts.title: Nicotine Addiction Risk in Adolescents
facts.description: Approximately 50% of adolescents who vape nicotine report symptoms of addiction or dependence
facts.trend: Adolescent brains are more susceptible to nicotine addiction due to ongoing development (prefrontal cortex)

facts.title: California Youth Using E-Cigarettes Daily
facts.description: 4.2% of California high school students report daily e-cigarette use
facts.trend: Daily use is a strong indicator of nicotine dependence

facts.title: Flavored E-Cigarettes Among Youth
facts.description: 73% of California youth who use e-cigarettes report using flavored products
facts.trend: Flavors significantly increase appeal to adolescents; marketing-driven

facts.title: Marijuana Use Health Effects (Adolescent Brains)
facts.description: Regular marijuana use during adolescence can impair developing brain functions, particularly memory consolidation, attention span, and impulse control
facts.trend: Effects can persist even after cessation; critical window for intervention is ages 12-21
facts.source: NIH National Institute on Drug Abuse

facts.title: Dual Use: Nicotine + Marijuana Among CA Youth
facts.description: 3.8% of California high school students report using both nicotine and marijuana in the past 30 days
facts.trend: Dual use increases health risks and addiction severity

facts.title: Long-term Health Effects of Nicotine Vaping
facts.description: Recent research shows nicotine vaping increases risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and heart disease even in adolescents
facts.trend: New research emerging on long-term vascular damage from e-cigarette use

facts.title: California Schools Reporting Vaping on Campus
facts.description: 85% of California public schools report observing or having confiscated e-cigarettes or vaping devices from students
facts.trend: High prevalence in schools drives need for interventions like YVAPE

facts.title: Awareness: Teen Perception of Nicotine Vaping Risks
facts.description: Only 58% of California high school students perceive regular e-cigarette use as harmful
facts.trend: Marketing and 'safer than cigarettes' messaging creates false perception of safety

facts.title: THC Potency in Vaping Products
facts.demographic: Commercial vape cartridges sold in CA
facts.description: Modern THC vape cartridges contain 60-90% THC (vs. 5-15% in traditional marijuana), significantly increasing risk of psychological dependence
facts.trend: Product potency has increased 5-10x in past decade
facts.source: California Department of Cannabis Regulation & SAMHSA

facts.title: Adolescent Brain Development (Ages 12-19)
facts.description: The prefrontal cortex (responsible for decision-making, impulse control, risk assessment) doesn't fully develop until age 25, making adolescents more susceptible to addiction
facts.trend: Neuroscience supports critical intervention window during YVAPE target age group
facts.source: NIH National Institute of Mental Health

facts.title: Success of Evidence-Based Interventions Like YVAPE
facts.description: Research shows evidence-based, supportive coaching programs like YVAPE achieve 35-45% quit rates among adolescents, vs. ~5% self-quit rate
facts.trend: Structured, compassionate intervention significantly outperforms willpower alone

nicotineVaping.notes: Significant progress due to FDA restrictions on flavored products and increased education; still substantial problem

marijuanaUse.notes: Increased access due to legalization; higher potency products contribute to rising use

marijuanaVaping.notes: Fastest-growing category; high-potency THC products make vaping attractive

dualUse.notes: Portion using both nicotine and marijuana; compounds addiction risk

key_factors: Legal marijuana market increases accessibility & product variety
Vape product marketing heavily targets youth (especially through social media)
Socioeconomic disparities in substance use rates
School enforcement varies widely by district
policy_efforts: Flavored e-cigarette restrictions (limited at state level, city-by-city enforcement)
